title: The Gravy Boat
trend: TikTok Chipmunks Dance (groups of three doing a short goofy routine to a sped-up, high-pitched remix; New Engen TikTok list, updated Nov 16 2026, US) + family holiday videos — teen Zoe drags her dad Lionel and Uncle Pete into the three-person dance while the speaker plays the song fast and high; they fail at bouncing, spinning and the silly face; twist: slowed down, it is the old record from Cousin Rhonda's wedding in nineteen ninety one — the dance is the one Grandma invented and they danced in matching vests (the gravy boat), and they have been warming up, not failing; button: Grandma arrives with her spoon and someone is getting cut from the group of three
youtube_title: I taught my dad and uncle the new three person dance. Then I slowed down the song 🕺
description:
Zoe needs her dad and Uncle Pete for a three person dance before tonight. Their shoulders do not go up and their silly faces look like they are waiting for a plumber. Then somebody slows the song down.

#cartoon #animation #funny #dance #shorts
tiktok_caption: i taught my dad and uncle the new three person dance. then i slowed down the song 🕺 #cartoon #animation #funny #dance

lines.text: Okay, old men. Three people, one dance, forty seconds. We post it tonight.
Old men? I am forty nine. That is basically a teenager with a mortgage.
Hello. I am the speaker. I play the song very fast and very high. It is my gift.
Why is it so high? It sounds like three hamsters won a car.
That is the point, Uncle Pete. Everybody does it in groups of three.
Step one. Shoulders up, shoulders down. Little bounce.
My shoulders do not go up anymore. They go up once a year. At tax time.
Starting the song now. Please hold on to something.
Bounce, bounce, point, point, spin.
I spun. The room did not stop spinning. Is that part of it?
It is now. Everyone is part of it.
Uncle Pete. You went left. Everybody went right.
I went left with confidence. That is called a solo.
Step two. The silly face. Puff your cheeks like a little animal.
Like this?
Dad, that is not a little animal. That is a man waiting for a plumber.
I have seen many faces. That one called the plumber twice.
I am trying. My cheeks are not in the group chat.
Okay. Full run. Phone is recording. Do not be weird.
Song starting. The tiny singers are ready.
Bounce, point, wait. Wait. Pete. Do you hear that?
Oh no. Lionel. I know this song.
You do not know this song. It came out this month.
Speaker. Play it slower. Much slower. Like a Sunday.
Slowing down. Slower. Oh. Oh my. That is a grown man singing.
That is the song from Cousin Rhonda's wedding. Nineteen ninety one.
We danced to it with Grandma. The three of us. In matching vests.
No. No, it is new. It is a new fast song.
It is an old slow song in a hurry. Like your father on a Monday.
Somebody found our old record and played it too fast. That is all this is.
And the dance. Shoulders up, little bounce, point, spin.
That was our dance. Grandma made it up. She called it the gravy boat.
You have been pretending you could not do it for ten minutes?
We were not pretending. We were warming up. We are forty nine.
Okay. Then show me. The real way. At the real speed.
Playing at wedding speed.
Shoulders up. Shoulders down. Slow bounce. Point to Grandma.
And the spin. And the dip. Nobody dips anymore. Shame.
Wait. That is actually good. Why is that actually good?
Because we practiced in the garage for a whole summer. No phone. Just Grandma with a spoon.
Three people. One dance. It was always three people.
Okay. We post it. The three of us. Matching vests.
The vests do not fit, Zoe. Nothing from nineteen ninety one fits.
Mine fits. As a hat.
Recording. Three, two, one.
Wait. Who is that at the door?
Oh no. Grandma heard the song.
She has her spoon. Somebody is getting kicked out of the group of three.
It is you, Lionel. It was always going to be you.
